messages.subject: Re: Build error of gcc-bridge-plugin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jens,

Renjin now relies on GCC to compile some Fortran/C math routines to JVM bytecode. One of this new build chain is a plugin for gcc that needs to be built-- and this is what's failing in your build.

The documentation needs to be updated for this, but in the meantime, some caveats:

- Compilation of C/Fortran code has been tested with GCC 4.6.3 on Linux. Other versions of GCC may not work, as I know the internal structure can change significantly between releases. I have tried and failed to get the gcc-bridge toolchain working on Cygwin, but have been unsuccessful.

- To build the GCC plugin itself, you need to install the plugin headers (on Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install build-essentials gcc-4.6-plugin-dev gfortran)

- GCC is only required at the build stage, the resulting JVM classes are fully platform independent.

That should do it.

In the future, I'm going to try to separate the GCC-built components out from the pure-Java components so that you can rely on existing builds of the C/Fortran while recompiling the Java sources on any platform.

If you run into any more problems, just post back here and we'll use it to get some good docs written.

Thanks!

Alex

Ah sorry I didn't realize you were using as a library.

If you're using Renjin as a Java library, you just need to include as org.renjin:renjin-script-engine as a dependency and Maven will resolve the transitive dependencies by itself. If you're using Ant or something else to build your project, then you might consider using Ivy to resolve dependencies.

But if you just want to do it manually, it should suffice to put renjin-script-engine.jar and the jars from the zip file on your class path.

I will add another assembly to the build that produces a nice zip file of all of renjin script engine's dependencies for those not using a dependency manager.
(http://code.google.com/p/renjin/issues/detail?id=55)

Best,
Alex

Alex
